brief: Goldman FICC's Chryssafis links disappointing megacap AI earnings (Tesla capex cuts, Meta's CDS at a record, weak Lam Research guidance) to three markets. Positioning: hedge funds hit record two-week net selling of Global Info Tech (-3.3 SD) with short leverage at the 99th percentile, so recent AI bounces look like short-covering. Credit: Goldman stays underweight USD IG Tech and neutral HY but expects high dispersion in project-finance bonds, where 2026 YTD issuance (~$105bn, about 4x 2020's pre-AI record) is almost all data centers; Bernstein sees a $76bn CoreWeave funding hole. Separately, Gulf escalation risk (Iran strike plans, Houthi attacks, Aramco evacuating Dhahran) pushed Brent higher; Goldman's scenarios range from mid-$70s to $140+ by 2027. Despite that, Treasury yields are falling because the bond market treats the AI de-rating as the more durable shock; since Oct 14 the AI basket's correlations with yields and USDJPY flipped sign, so Goldman likes equities-down/yields-down hedges and sees cheap USDJPY puts (yen ~40% undervalued per GSDEER) as the trade, reasoning an AI scare would trigger Japanese repatriation. French OAT/Bund spreads hit a record 173bps, which Goldman says needs energy relief to compress.
